Chapter 13: Praying for Peace in Times of Conflict.
You know, conflict is just a part of life. It shows up between siblings, with partners, at work, and even within our families. For parents, there’s almost nothing harder than watching your grown children struggle with tension, or even drift apart. The urge to step in, to smooth things over, to make everything right—it’s so strong. But sometimes, no matter how hard you try, peace seems just out of reach.
Imagine a mother, heartbroken because her two sons aren’t speaking. She feels trapped in the middle, desperate to bring them back together. Every attempt she makes seems to push them further apart. Eventually, she turns to prayer. Not just asking for her sons to forgive each other, but for humility, for the courage to keep reaching out, and for her own heart to soften.
Most of us don’t realize that peace is more than just a moment—it’s a choice, a process, even a journey. You can’t force reconciliation, but you can open the door to it. For parents, learning to let go can be one of the toughest lessons. That’s where prayer really comes in. It becomes a way to hold onto hope, to trust that healing can happen, even if you can’t see the path just yet.
Take a father, for example, watching his daughter struggle with a tough situation at work. He feels powerless to protect her, but he prays—for wisdom, for patience, for her to have the grace to handle whatever comes her way. Over time, things start to shift. The pressure eases, relationships at work soften, and little by little, peace finds its way back.
Conflict isn’t something any of us can completely avoid. But as parents, you can pray for open hearts, for the strength to forgive, and for the willingness to really listen and understand. It’s about trusting that even the deepest wounds can be healed.
And here’s the key takeaway: Peace is always possible—even when it feels far away. Sometimes, the most powerful thing you can do is simply pray, and hold on to hope.
